d_sv_content.name: Assessing a new technique to shrink liver tumors in dogs
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us learn more about this new technique that could shrink liver tumors in dogs!
d_sv_content.description:
When liver tumors in dogs cannot be removed with surgery, treatment options are limited or non-existent. In humans, one of the standard treatments for those cases is transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), which eliminates the blood supply of the tumor and may decrease tumor size. The objectives of this study are to 1) describe the procedure of TACE  using a novel treatment agent in a group of dogs with naturally-occurring liver cancer, and 2) evaluate the effect that liver TACE has on clinical signs, size and viability of the tumor.

Demonstrating the feasibility and efficacy of liver TACE to improve clinical signs and decrease tumor size and volume can significantly advance our treatment of this difficult disease process, as current treatment options are limited and lack efficacy. Additionally, liver TACE is minimally invasive and provides many potential advantages over traditional surgical therapies.
d_sv_content.requirements: If you agree to have your dog participate in this study, the following procedures will occur:* CT scan and TACE while under anesthesia* A second CT scan approximately 4 weeks post-TACE* Hospitalization for 1-2 days post treatment pending response to treatment* Completion of questionnaires
d_sv_content.responsibilities: If you allow your dog to participate in this study, you will be responsible for keeping all scheduled appointments, completing several questionnaires, and covering costs associated with the TACE procedure and any complications that may occur as part of that procedure.
d_sv_content.benefits: We hope that the data acquired in this study will allow us to advance the treatment of cancer in both pets and people.
d_sv_content.compensation: The client is responsible for paying for the liver transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) procedure and any complications that may occur as part of that procedure. There is no charge for you to allow your dog to participate in this clinical trial. All costs directly associated with the study will be paid by the trial, including exams, diagnostic tests and CT scans.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: Your dog will be enrolled in the study for approximately 1 month.
